name: Jaisalmer Fort
alt: Aerial view of Jaisalmer Fort in Jaisalmer, Rajasthan, India
caption: Jaisalmer Fort, the 'Golden Fort', is one of the world's few living forts, with homes, shops and temples still inside its sandstone walls.
tags: India; Rajasthan; Jaisalmer; Jaisalmer Fort; Sonar Qila; Thar Desert; Hill Forts of Rajasthan; Aerial Photography; Drone Photography
prompt: Aerial photograph of Jaisalmer Fort, Rajasthan: a living hilltop citadel of weathered pale straw-yellow sandstone crowning Trikuta Hill above the Thar Desert. A rugged outer wall of rough-cut sandstone blocks traces the rim of the hill, broken into dozens of squat rounded bastions, their faces streaked, chipped and stained darker beneath the parapets. Within the walls hundreds of flat-roofed sandstone houses climb in uneven tiers, divided by narrow shadowed lanes, with carved haveli facades and latticed jharokha balconies, rooftop water tanks, satellite dishes, laundry and parked scooters, and a few small carved Jain temple spires rising slightly above a flat horizontal skyline. Below the hill the town spreads in low, irregular sandstone and sun-faded plaster buildings, a curving road with a few cars, motorcycles and a bus, scattered khejri trees, stony slopes with boulders, then flat beige desert fading into dust haze. Shot from 120 m above, south-west of the hill, camera tilted 30° downward, 32mm lens. Late-afternoon sun from the left, long soft shadows between the bastions, pale hazy sky. name: Pangong Lake
alt: Aerial view of Pangong Lake in Ladakh, India
caption: Pangong Lake, at about 4,200 m in Ladakh, shifts through shades of blue and stretches across the border into Tibet.
tags: India; Ladakh; Pangong Lake; Pangong Tso; Himalayas; High-altitude Lake; Aerial Photography; Drone Photography
prompt: Aerial photograph of Pangong Lake in eastern Ladakh at about 4,200 m: a long, narrow ribbon of water stretching east between bare Himalayan ranges until it fades into haze. Near the shore the water is clear pale green-turquoise over a pebbly bed of grey and ochre stones, then bands into teal and deep slate-blue further out, textured with fine wind ripples; a thin white line of wave wash edges the gravel beach. Steep, angular mountains of fractured grey, brown and rust-coloured rock rise from the water, with layered strata, broken cliffs, long scree slopes, talus fans and dry gullies; a thin dusting of snow lies on the highest distant summit. A narrow dirt track follows the shore past a few low whitewashed flat-roofed Ladakhi houses with firewood stacked on the roofs, a cluster of small canvas tents and one dusty SUV casting a sharp shadow. Shot from 160 m above the western shore near Spangmik, camera tilted 20° downward, 24mm lens.
